text:
maria: FYI I opened a tiny docs PR to patch SDK snippets and add a smoke test for the TritonX model entry. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4599
kevin: nice. which variant are we touching?
sanjeev: is this about the quantized KV-cache behaviour we saw in infra?
maria: exactly. tritonx-6b-quant has a KV warmup quirk at long contexts; I added a short compatibility note and a fallback snippet.
elaine: can you paste the smoke commands? I'll run quick locally.
maria: run in repo root: ```bash
pytest tests/smoke/test_tritonx.py::test_kv_warmup -q
# or quick check: python tools/model_check.py --model tritonx-6b-quant --seq 2048
```
kevin: reminder: snippets must use the new SDK import path (sdk v3). devex warned about that change.
devex: yes — update `from rw.sdk import Client` -> `from redwood import Client`. left a comment on the PR for consistency across snippets.
sanjeev: also swap the benchmark link; current model card links to cpu-only bench. should point to GPU profile: https://bench.redwood.ai/tritonx-6b/gpu-profile.json
maria: noted, I put the GPU link in the draft but left the old link commented. will remove the comment and update text.
elaine: running tests now... got a FAIL on kv warmup token mismatch when seq>1024. stack shows different token stream after warmup.
kevin: that matches infra findings. propose a short inline note: "KV cache warmup may diverge for seq > 1024 on TritonX quantized builds; use fallback to fp16 or set KV_WARMUP_STEPS=32."
maria: draft fallback snippet: ```yaml
variant: tritonx-6b-quant
fallback: tritonx-6b-fp16
env: KV_WARMUP_STEPS=32
```
sanjeev: add an SDK example too: ```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
resp = client.generate(
  model='tritonx-6b-quant',
  prompt='hello',
  fallback_policy={'model':'tritonx-6b-fp16','env':{'KV_WARMUP_STEPS':'32'}}
)
```
devex: small lint note: runtime expects `fallback_policy` indeed. and prefer double quotes in YAML snippets for CI parsing.
maria: fixed both in PR. I also added a one-line note about expected throughput drop at seq > 2000 with link to perf dashboard.
kevin: can we add a tiny regression that checks deterministic output for two short prompts after warmup? keeps CI quick.
elaine: added a lightweight assertion locally, smoke tests now pass with fallback config. I'll paste results as a gist into the PR.
docs-bot: CI: docs-smoke-tests passed (4/4) — https://ci.redwood.ai/4599/logs
maria: awesome, thanks everyone. next steps: kevin review SDK snippets, sanjeev validate perf link and wording. target merge today. ping @kevin @devex if blocked. :rocket:
